thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stocks Resilient After Tepid As Consumer Staples Rally

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: U.S. Stocks Resilient After Tepid As Consumer Staples Rally
text:
By Anora M. Gaudiano and Mark economy added 157,000 jobs in July, compared with 195,000 forecast
U.S. stocks were resilient Friday with the S&P 500 and the Dow trading higher after the July jobs report came in below expectations, though a drop in the unemployment rate and increases to the previous two months indicate the labor market remains healthy.
Investors also grappled with news that China would retaliate with tariffs on $60 billion in U.S. goods, at a time when trade deficit rose for the first time in four months.
What are benchmarks doing?
The S&P 500 rose 8 points, or 0.3%, to 2,835, with nine of its 11 sectors trading higher. Consumer staples shares were leading the gains, up more than 1%. The benchmark index was on track for a 0.6% weekly gain.
The Nasdaq Composite Index switched between small gains and losses, last trading down 4 points to 7,798, taking a breather after a 1.2% rally fueled by Apple Inc.'s (AAPL) share advance on Thursday.
Apple made history to become the first U.S. company to reach a valuation of $1 trillion (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-1-trillion-heres-the-meltdown-that-followed-the-first-company-to-get-there-2018-08-01), following its better-than-expected quarterly results.
The tech-heavy index is on track for a 0.8% weekly gain.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 91 points, or 0.4% to 25,417 but is set to finish the week slightly lower.
What's driving markets?
Wall Street has been caught up in a battle between concerns over the U.S.'s trade spats with China and optimism over economic and corporate earnings that have been outstanding by most measures.
The market reaction to Friday's July nonfarm payrolls report was largely muted. The annualized rate of wage gains was unchanged at 2.7%, suggesting no immediate pressure on inflation.
The Federal Reserve's latest policy update affirmed the central bank's plan to raise interest rates at least once more this year, and the jobs report wasn't seen as likely to change that narrative. The central bank is next expected to raise interest rates in September.

What are analysts are saying?
"The latest jobs reports means that the economy is chugging along, we are still adding jobs this late in the cycle while we had double-digit revenue and earnings growth," said Michael Antonelli, equity sales trader at Robert W. Baird & Co.
"It looks as though the risk to trade wars is asymmetric to upside. All the bad news is priced in, but if we get some kind of resolution with China, then markets will rip higher," Antonelli said.
What else is on investors' radar?
The trade deficit rose 7% in June trade-deficit-climbs-7-still-on-track-to-hit-10-year-high-2018-08-03)to mark the first increase in four months, keeping the U.S. on track to post the largest annual gap in a decade even as the Trump White House escalates tariffs in an effort to bring it down.
The ISM non-manufacturing index (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ism-services-index-in-july-falls-to-11-month-low-2018-08-03) in July slipped to 55.7%, underperforming consensus estimates.
Elsewhere, investors are watching signs of economic slowdown in China. A private gauge showed service sector activity in the country continued to grow in July, but at a slower pace than in June (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/chinas-caixin-pmi-shows-services-activity-cooling-2018-08-03). China's economy, already facing a slide, has been hurt by the tariff clash with the U.S.
Key Chinese equity index the Shanghai Composite fell 1%, while the Shenzhen Composite declined by 1.7% after hitting a 3 1/2 -year closing low in the prior session.
Which stocks are in focus?
Dish Network Corp. (DISH)soared (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dish-networks-stock-soars-as-earnings-and-revenue-beat-expectations-2018-08-03) 13% after the satellite pay-TV service reported better-than-expected second-quarter earnings and revenue.
Kraft Heinz Co. (KHC) climbed 8.3% after reporting second-quarter earnings.
Shares of CBS Corp. (CBSA) were flat after the media company late Thursday reported second-quarter earnings that came in below expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cbs-shares-down-slightly-after-media-company-misses-expectations-2018-08-02) but narrowly topped revenue forecasts for the quarter. CBS on Wednesday said its board of directors had hired outside lawyers to conduct an investigation into allegations that Chief Executive Les Moonves had sexually harassed women. Thursday's earnings statement made no mention (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/cbs-earnings-call-oddly-silent-on-allegations-against-moonves-2018-08-02) of Moonves' status.
Shares of Groupon Inc.(GRPN) bounced back to advance after the company posted weaker-than-expected second-quarter results (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/groupon-stock-falls-after-earnings-revenue-miss-expectations-2018-08-03).
What are other markets doing?
Oil futures (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-climbs-and-extends-climb-above-6-week-low-2018-08-03) reversed earlier gains and were trading lower and are likely to finish the week with losses. Gold futures (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gold-at-risk-of-booking-3-session-skid-as-jobs-report-looms-2018-08-03) settled higher and the U.S. dollar index (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-dips-ahead-of-jobs-report-2018-08-03) recovered from earlier loss to trade flat.
European stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-recover-ground-lifted-by-tech-sector-2018-08-03) rose, while Asian markets finished mixed.
--Sue Chang contributed to this report
